grammar.title: 3A: Choosing between comparatives and superlatives
grammar.explanation:
A **comparative adjective** compares two people or things, like two teams. Use it with the word **than**.

Make a comparative by adding **-er** to short adjectives, like faster. Use **more** before long adjectives, like more difficult.

Watch the spelling: big becomes **bigger**, and easy becomes **easier**. Two adjectives are irregular: **good → better** and **bad → worse**.

When two things are equal, use **(not) as + adjective + as**. You can compare two scores, two matches, or two coaches this way.

A **superlative adjective** compares one thing with a whole group, like one team in a match. Always use **the** before it.

Make a superlative by adding **-est** to short adjectives, like fastest. Use **the most** before long adjectives, like the most difficult.

After a superlative, use **in**, never of. Think of the best goal in the match, or the best stretch in your exercise.

Now you know ten sports words for practice: team, match, coach, practice, goal, score, exercise, muscle, stretch, and balance.
examples: Our team is *faster than* their team. (comparative + than)
Stretching is *more difficult than* running. (more + long adjective)
Our coach is *better than* their coach. (irregular: good → better)
My muscle is *bigger than* last month. (spelling: double the last letter)
My balance is *as good as* yours. (as + adjective + as)
This exercise is *the easiest* in my practice. (superlative + -est)
He is *the tallest* player on the team. (always use the)
She scored *the best* goal in the match. (superlative + in)
Our score is *higher than* last week's score. (comparative + -er)
Warm muscles work *better than* cold muscles. (irregular: good → better)

practice.q: Complete: My team is ___ (fast) than yours.
Complete: She is the ___ (good) player on the team.
Which is correct: 'the best goal in the match' or 'the best goal of the match'?
practice.a: 'the best goal in the match' — use in, not of, after a superlative.
